china-1926-7:p0570_1.rationale: Annual output of one-cent copper coins is a coinage and currency issuance series, not general manufacturing.

china-1926-7:p0571_1.rationale: Copper-cents per dollar at Shanghai, 1912-1925, show depreciation of the copper currency against the dollar. The rate is an exchange rate between two coins within one monetary system.
review_questions: The foreign-exchange tag was not used because the rates compare domestic coin denominations rather than foreign currencies; confirm.

china-1926-7:p0571_2.rationale: Percentage loss on converting copper-cent income into dollars shows copper-coin depreciation; the Shanghai Tramways appear only as the source of the data.

china-1926-7:p0572_1.rationale: Customs totals of silver bar and sycee imports and exports, 1892-1924, are a bullion trade series with net imports. No silver tag fits because silver here is bullion trade tied to currency use, not mining or a commodity-output table.
review_questions: Should the silver tag cover bullion trade as well as mining and commodity data?

china-1926-7:p0572_2.rationale: Sources of silver bars reaching Shanghai over four years (imports from the U.S.A., London and Eastern ports) form a bullion import table.
review_questions: Should the silver tag cover bullion trade as well as mining and commodity data?

china-1926-7:p0572_3.rationale: Estimated uses of imported silver bars for coinage versus sycee and the arts bear on the monetary use of silver.

china-1926-7:p0573_1.rationale: Weights and fineness of the principal taels are monetary-unit standards and equivalents.

china-1926-7:p0573_2.rationale: A conversion table giving the proceeds in Shanghai taels of 100,000 troy ounces of bar silver at different finenesses. It converts between silver standards and tael units.

china-1926-7:p0575_1.rationale: Gross weight, fineness and fine-silver content of the dollar coins current in China are metallic-content currency data.

china-1926-7:p0577_1.rationale: Customs values of gold imported into and exported from China, 1890-1924, are a gold trade series. Under the rules, gold trade takes the gold tag, which is ordinarily paired with exports.
